title.zh: 卷七十九 列傳第十七: 酈瓊 李成 孔彥舟 徐文 施宜生 張中孚 張中彥 宇文虛中 王倫
title.en: Volume 79 Biographies 17: Li Qiong, Li Cheng, Kong Yanzhou, Xu Wen, Shi Yisheng, Zhang Zhongfu, Zhang Zhongyan, Yu Wenxuzhong, Wang Lun
title.raw: 卷七十九 列傳第十七: 酈瓊 李成 孔彥舟 徐文 施宜生 張中孚 張中彥 宇文虛中 王倫 Volume 79 Biographies 17: Li Qiong, Li Cheng, Kong Yanzhou, Xu Wen, Shi Yisheng, Zhang Zhongfu, Zhang Zhongyan, Yu Wenxuzhong, Wang Lun

sentences.zh: 列傳第十七 ○酈瓊 李成 孔彥舟 徐文 施宜生 張中孚 張中彥 宇文虛中 王倫

translations.literal: Biographies 17 ○ Li Qiong, Li Cheng, Kong Yanzhou, Xu Wen, Shi Yisheng, Zhang Zhongfu, Zhang Zhongyan, Yu Wen Xuzhong, Wang Lun
translations.idiomatic: Biography 17 — Li Qiong, Li Cheng, Kong Yanzhou, Xu Wen, Shi Yisheng, Zhang Zhongfu, Zhang Zhongyan, Yuwen Xuzhong, and Wang Lun

sentences.zh: 酈瓊，字國寶，相州臨漳人。

translations.literal: Li Qiong, courtesy name Guobao, was a native of Linzhang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong, whose courtesy name was Guobao, came from Linzhang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 補州學生。

translations.literal: He was enrolled as a prefectural student.
translations.idiomatic: He entered training as a prefectural student.

sentences.zh: 宋宣和間，盜賊起，瓊乃更學擊刺挽強，試弓馬，隸宗澤軍，駐於磁州。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe era of Song, when bandits rose up, Qiong then changed to studying thrusting, stabbing, and drawing the strong bow; he tested bow and horse skills and was attached to Zong Ze's army, stationed at Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits broke out during the Song Xuanhe period, Qiong turned to training in close combat and heavy archery, passed tests in mounted archery, and joined Zong Ze's army, which was stationed at Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾告歸，括集義軍七百人，複從澤，澤署瓊為七百人長。

translations.literal: Before long he asked leave to return home, gathered seven hundred righteous-army troops, and rejoined Ze; Ze appointed Qiong commander of the seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he took leave to return home, raised a force of seven hundred volunteer troops, and rejoined Zong Ze, who made Qiong their commander.

sentences.zh: 澤死，調戍滑州。

translations.literal: When Ze died, [Qiong] was transferred to garrison duty at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong Ze died, Qiong was reassigned to garrison Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 時宗望伐宋，將渡河。

translations.literal: At that time Zongwang was campaigning against Song and was about to cross the [Yellow] River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Zongwang was invading the Song and preparing to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 戍軍亂，殺其統制趙世彥，而推瓊為主。

translations.literal: The garrison troops mutinied, killed their commander Zhao Shiyan, and raised Qiong as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison mutinied, killed their commander Zhao Shiyan, and made Qiong their leader.

sentences.zh: 瓊因誘眾，號為勤王，行且收兵。

translations.literal: Qiong therefore incited the masses, declaring [the movement] for saving the throne, and marched while gathering troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong rallied the men under the banner of "rescuing the throne" and marched on, drawing more troops to him as he went.

sentences.zh: 比渡淮，有眾萬餘。

translations.literal: By the time he crossed the Huai, he had a force of more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he crossed the Huai, his following had grown to more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 康王以為楚州安撫使、淮南東路兵馬鈐轄，累遷武泰軍承宣使。

translations.literal: Prince Kang appointed him Pacification Commissioner of Chuzhou and Military Controller of Huainan East Circuit, with repeated promotion to honorary commissioner of the Wutai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang appointed him pacification commissioner of Chuzhou and military controller of Huainan East Circuit, and eventually promoted him to honorary commissioner of the Wutai Army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，率所領步騎十余萬附于齊，授靜難軍節度使，知拱州。

translations.literal: Before long, leading more than one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry under his command, he submitted to Qi and was given the post of military governor of the Jingnan Army and administrative charge of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he led his force of more than a hundred thousand foot and horse soldiers over to Qi, and was appointed military governor of the Jingnan Army with administrative charge of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，以為博州防禦使。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was abolished, he was made defensive commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was abolished, he was made defensive commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 用廉，遷驃騎上將軍。

translations.literal: [For] employing integrity, he was transferred to chief general of the Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for integrity, he was promoted to chief general of the Flying Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複河南，以瓊為山東路弩手千戶，知亳州事。

translations.literal: When Zongbi recovered Henan, Qiong was made commander of a thousand crossbowmen on the Shandong Circuit and given charge of Bozhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi reconquered Henan, Qiong was made commander of a thousand crossbowmen on the Shandong route and put in charge of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，去官。

translations.literal: [Upon] completing mourning for his mother, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再伐江南，以瓊素知南方山川險易，召至軍與計事。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again campaigned against Jiangnan, because Qiong had long known the hazardous and easy points of southern mountains and rivers, he was summoned to the army to consult on planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi launched another campaign against the south, he summoned Qiong to headquarters for planning because Qiong had long known the terrain and passes of the southern provinces.

sentences.zh: 從容語同列曰：「瓊嘗從大軍南伐，每見元帥國王親臨陣督戰，矢石交集，而王免胄，指麾三軍，意氣自若，用兵制勝，皆與孫、吳合，可謂命世雄材矣。

translations.literal: Speaking at ease to his colleagues, he said: "Qiong once followed the great army south in campaign; each time I saw the marshal prince personally come to the front to supervise battle, arrows and stones flying thick, yet the prince removed his helmet, directing the three armies, spirit calm as ever; wielding troops to secure victory, all in accord with Sun and Wu—truly a world-dominating hero.
translations.idiomatic: He said calmly to his colleagues, "I once marched south with the main army. Whenever our marshal prince came to the front in person to direct the fighting, arrows and stones flew everywhere, yet he would take off his helmet and command the three armies with perfect composure. The way he handled troops to win battles matched Sunzi and Wuzi—it was the work of a once-in-an-age champion.

sentences.zh: 至於親冒鋒鏑，進不避難，將士視之，孰敢愛死乎。

translations.literal: As for personally braving blades and arrows, advancing without avoiding danger—when soldiers see this, who would dare spare his life?
translations.idiomatic: When the commander himself faces blades and arrows and never flinches, what soldier watching him will hold back his life?

sentences.zh: 宜其所向無前，日辟國千里也。

translations.literal: No wonder he met no equal wherever he advanced and daily opened territory a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder he swept all before him and daily extended the realm by a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 江南諸帥，才能不及中人。

translations.literal: The various commanders of Jiangnan have talent not reaching even the mediocre.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commanders in the south are barely average in ability.

sentences.zh: 每當出兵，必身居數百裏外，謂之持重。

translations.literal: Whenever they send out troops, they always personally stay hundreds of li away, calling it "holding weight" (caution).
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they take the field, they stay hundreds of li to the rear and call it "prudence."

sentences.zh: 或督召軍旅，易置將校，僅以一介之士持虛文諭之，謂之調發。

translations.literal: Or when supervising and summoning armies, they readily replace officers, sending merely a single messenger bearing empty documents to instruct them, calling it "mobilization."
translations.idiomatic: When they need armies, they shuffle officers at will and dispatch a lone clerk with written orders—this they call "mobilization."

sentences.zh: 制敵決勝委之偏裨，是以智者解體，愚者喪師。

translations.literal: Entrusting control of the enemy and decision of victory to subordinate commanders, so the wise lose heart and the foolish lose armies.
translations.idiomatic: They leave defeating the enemy to junior officers, so the capable lose heart and the foolish lose their armies.

sentences.zh: 幸一小捷，則露布飛馳，增加俘級以為己功，斂怨將士。

translations.literal: If by chance a small victory, then victory reports fly swift, inflating captives and head counts as personal merit, gathering resentment from officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: If they score even a small victory, they rush out victory bulletins and pad the prisoner and kill counts to claim credit, breeding resentment among their troops.

sentences.zh: 縱或親臨，亦必先遁。

translations.literal: Even if they personally come [to the field], they also flee first.
translations.idiomatic: Even when they appear in person, they are first to flee.

sentences.zh: 而又國政不綱，才有微功，已加厚賞，或有大罪，乃置而不誅。

translations.literal: Moreover the statecraft lacks order: slight merit receives heavy reward, while great crime is overlooked and unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Their government is in disorder too—petty merit wins lavish rewards, while great crimes go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 不即覆亡，已為天幸，何能振起耶？」

translations.literal: If they do not immediately perish, that is already heaven's favor—how could they revive?"
translations.idiomatic: That they have not already collapsed is sheer luck—how could they possibly recover?"

sentences.zh: 眾以為確論。

translations.literal: The assembly regarded this as sound doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present took this for the truth.

sentences.zh: 元帥，謂宗弼也。

translations.literal: "Marshal" refers to Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: "The marshal" here means Zongbi.

sentences.zh: 及宗弼問瓊以江南成敗，誰敢相拒者。

translations.literal: When Zongbi asked Qiong about success and failure in Jiangnan, who would dare to resist?
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi asked Qiong about the prospects in Jiangnan, no one would dare stand in their way.

sentences.zh: 瓊曰：「江南軍勢怯弱，皆敗亡之餘，又無良帥，何以禦我。

translations.literal: Qiong said: "Jiangnan's military strength is timid and weak, all remnants of defeat and ruin, and without good commanders—how could they oppose us?
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said, "The southern armies are weak and cowardly—remnants of defeated forces with no capable commanders. How could they resist us?

sentences.zh: 頗聞秦檜當國用事。

translations.literal: I have often heard that Qin Gui holds state power.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that Qin Gui holds power in the government.

sentences.zh: 檜，老儒，所謂亡國之大夫，兢兢自守，惟顛覆是懼。

translations.literal: Gui is an old Confucian, what is called a minister of a state about to perish, anxiously guarding himself, fearing only overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Gui is an elderly scholar-official of the sort that ruins kingdoms—cautious to the point of paralysis, terrified only of losing power.

sentences.zh: 吾以大軍臨之，彼之君臣，方且心破膽裂，將哀鳴不暇，蓋傷弓之鳥可以虛弦下也。」

translations.literal: When our great army presses on them, their ruler and ministers will have hearts broken and gall split, scarcely able to wail in time—like a bird wounded by the bow, it can be brought down by an empty bowstring."
translations.idiomatic: When our great army reaches them, their ruler and ministers will be heartsick with terror—they will barely have time to beg for mercy. They are like birds wounded by an arrow: even an empty bowstring will bring them down."

sentences.zh: 既而江南果稱臣，宗弼喜瓊為知言。

translations.literal: Before long Jiangnan indeed submitted as vassal; Zongbi was pleased that Qiong had spoken to the point.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward the south did in fact submit as a vassal, and Zongbi was delighted that Qiong had judged the situation correctly.

sentences.zh: 初，瓊去亳未幾，宋兵陷之而不守，複棄去，乃以州人宋超守之。

translations.literal: Earlier, not long after Qiong left Bo, Song troops took it but did not hold it and abandoned it again; the local man Song Chao was then put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, not long after Qiong left Bo, Song troops took it but did not hold it and abandoned it again. The local man Song Chao was then put in charge.

sentences.zh: 及大軍至，超複以州事委其鈐轄衛經而遁去。

translations.literal: When the great army arrived, Chao again entrusted the prefectural administration to his controller Wei Jing and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army arrived, Chao again entrusted the prefectural administration to his controller Wei Jing and fled.

sentences.zh: 帥府使人招經，經不下。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters sent men to summon Jing, but he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters sent men to summon Jing, but he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 及城潰，百姓惶懼待命，瓊請于元帥曰：「城所不下者，凶豎劫之也。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the people were fearful and awaited their fate; Qiong requested of the marshal: "The reason the city would not submit is that wicked men held it hostage.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the people were fearful and awaited their fate. Qiong said to the marshal, "The reason the city would not submit is that wicked men held it hostage.

sentences.zh: 民何罪，願慰安之。」

translations.literal: What crime have the people committed? I beg that they be reassured and comforted."
translations.idiomatic: What crime have the people committed? I beg that they be reassured and comforted."

sentences.zh: 元帥以瓊先嘗守亳，因止戮經而釋其州人，複命瓊守亳。

translations.literal: Because Qiong had formerly governed Bo, the marshal therefore stopped the execution of Jing and released the people of the prefecture, again ordering Qiong to govern Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qiong had formerly governed Bo, the marshal stopped the execution of Jing, released the people of the prefecture, and again ordered Qiong to govern Bo.

sentences.zh: 凡六年，亳人德之。

translations.literal: For six years in all the people of Bo were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: For six years in all the people of Bo were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 遷武甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 八年，為泰甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he became military governor of the Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became military governor of the Taining Army.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷歸德尹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to intendant of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to intendant of Guide.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，加金紫光祿大夫，卒于官，年五十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Tassel; he died in office at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Tassel. He died in office at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 李成，字伯友，雄州歸信人。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, courtesy name Boyou, was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, whose courtesy name was Boyou, came from Guixin in Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 勇力絕倫，能挽弓三百斤。

translations.literal: His courage and strength were unmatched; he could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: His courage and strength were unmatched—he could draw a bow weighing three hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 宋宣和初，試弓手，挽強異等。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuanhe era of Song, he tested as an archer and ranked highest in drawing the strong bow.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song Xuanhe period he tested as an archer and ranked highest in drawing the heavy bow.

sentences.zh: 累官淮南招捉使。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to Pacification Commissioner for Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become pacification commissioner for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 成乃聚眾為盜，鈔掠江南，宋遣兵破之，成遂歸齊，累除知開德府，從大軍伐宋。

translations.literal: Cheng then gathered a band of raiders and plundered Jiangnan; Song sent troops to defeat him, and Cheng then submitted to Qi; he was repeatedly made administrative chief of Kaide Prefecture and followed the great army against Song.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then gathered a band and raided Jiangnan; Song sent troops to defeat him, after which he submitted to Qi, was repeatedly made prefect of Kaide, and joined the main army in campaigns against the Song.

sentences.zh: 齊廢，再除安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished, he was again made military governor of the Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished, he was again appointed military governor of the Anwu Army.

sentences.zh: 成在降附諸將中最勇鷙，號令甚嚴，眾莫敢犯。

translations.literal: Among the surrendered generals, Cheng was the fiercest and most brutal; his commands were very strict and none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Among the surrendered generals, Cheng was the fiercest and most brutal; his commands were strict and none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 臨陣身先諸將。

translations.literal: In battle he took the lead ahead of all other generals.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he always led from the front, ahead of every other general.

sentences.zh: 士卒未食不先食，有病者親視之。

translations.literal: The soldiers would not eat before he ate; when any were ill he attended them personally.
translations.idiomatic: He would not eat until his soldiers had eaten, and when any fell ill he tended them himself.

sentences.zh: 不持雨具，雖沾濕自如也。

translations.literal: He carried no rain gear and was indifferent even when soaked through.
translations.idiomatic: He carried no rain gear and was untroubled even when drenched.

sentences.zh: 有告成反者，宗弼察其誣，使成自治，成杖而釋之，其不校如此。

translations.literal: When someone reported that Cheng was plotting rebellion, Zongbi saw it was slander and had Cheng settle it himself—Cheng beat the accuser and released him, so unconcerned about rivalry was he.
translations.idiomatic: When someone accused Cheng of plotting rebellion, Zongbi saw the charge was false and had Cheng handle the matter himself—Cheng beat the accuser and let him go, so little did he trouble himself over such slights.

sentences.zh: 以此士樂為用，所至克捷。

translations.literal: For this reason the troops were glad to serve him and wherever he went he won victories.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason his men were glad to follow him, and wherever he went he won victories.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再取河南，宋李興據河南府。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again took Henan, Song's Li Xing held Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi reconquered Henan, the Song general Li Xing held Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 成引軍入孟津。

translations.literal: Cheng led his army into Mengjin.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng led his army into Mengjin.

sentences.zh: 興率眾薄城，鼓噪請戰，成不應。

translations.literal: Xing led his force to press the city, clamoring for battle with drums and shouts, but Cheng did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Xing led his troops up to the walls, beating drums and shouting for battle, but Cheng did not respond.

sentences.zh: 日下昃，興士卒倦且饑，成開門急擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When the sun declined westward, Xing's soldiers were weary and hungry; Cheng opened the gates and struck hard, routing them completely.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun was low in the west, Xing's soldiers were weary and hungry; Cheng opened the gates and struck hard, routing them completely.

sentences.zh: 興走漢南，成遂取洛陽、嵩、汝等。

translations.literal: Xing fled to the south of the Han River; Cheng then took Luoyang, Song, Ru, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xing fled south of the Han, and Cheng then took Luoyang, Song, Ru, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 河南平，宗弼奏成為河南尹，都管押本路兵馬。

translations.literal: When Henan was pacified, Zongbi memorialized making Cheng Henan Intendant and commander-in-chief of local military forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan was pacified, Zongbi recommended Cheng as intendant of Henan and overall commander of military forces on that circuit.

sentences.zh: 嘗取官羨粟充公費，坐奪兩官，解職。

translations.literal: Once he used official salary grain to cover public expenses and was punished by demotion of two ranks and removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Once he used official salary grain to cover public expenses and was demoted two ranks and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 正隆間，起為真定尹，封郡王，例封濟國公。

translations.literal: During the Zhenglong era he was recalled as intendant of Zhending, enfeoffed as a prince of a commandery—by precedent enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenglong era he was recalled as intendant of Zhending and enfeoffed as a commandery prince—in accordance with precedent, as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 孔彥舟

translations.literal: Kong Yanzhou
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yanzhou

sentences.zh: 孔彥舟，字巨濟，相州林慮人。

translations.literal: Kong Yanzhou, courtesy name Juji, was a native of Linlu in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yanzhou, whose courtesy name was Juji, came from Linlu in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 亡賴，不事生產，避罪之汴，占籍軍中。

translations.literal: A wastrel who would not engage in productive work, he fled to Bian to escape punishment and enrolled in the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: A wastrel who would not work for a living, he fled to Bian to escape punishment and enrolled in the army rolls.

sentences.zh: 坐事系獄，說守者解其縛，乘夜逾城遁去。

translations.literal: Imprisoned for an offense, he persuaded his guard to untie him, and by night escaped over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned for an offense, he persuaded his guard to untie him and escaped over the wall by night.

sentences.zh: 已而殺人，亡命為盜。

translations.literal: Thereafter he killed a man and took to the hills as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed a man and took to the hills as an outlaw.

sentences.zh: 宋靖康初，應募，累官京東西路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: Early in Jingkang of Song he enlisted and rose to Military Controller of the Jingdong and Jingxi Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song Jingkang period he enlisted and eventually became military controller of the Jingdong and Jingxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 聞大軍將至山東，遂率所部，劫殺居民，燒廬舍，掠財物，渡河南去。

translations.literal: Hearing the great army was about to reach Shandong, he led his force, killing and plundering residents, burning houses, seizing goods, and crossed south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Jin main army was approaching Shandong, he led his troops south across the river, killing and plundering civilians, burning homes, and seizing goods as he went.

sentences.zh: 宋人複招之，以為沿江招捉使。

translations.literal: The Song again recruited him and made him Pacification Commissioner along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court recruited him again and made him pacification commissioner along the river.

sentences.zh: 彥舟暴橫，不奉約束，宋人將以兵執之，彥舟走之齊，從劉麟伐宋，為行軍都統，改行營左總管。

translations.literal: Yanzhou was violent and unrestrained, refusing orders; when the Song were about to arrest him with troops, Yanzhou fled to Qi, followed Liu Lin against Song as chief of the field army, and was changed to left chief of the mobile camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was violent and defied orders; when the Song prepared to seize him by force, he fled to Qi, followed Liu Lin in campaigns against the Song as chief of the field army, and was later made left chief of the mobile camp.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，累知淄州。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was abolished, he was repeatedly made prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished, he served repeatedly as prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 從宗弼取河南，克鄭州，擒其守劉政，破孟邦傑于登封，授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: Following Zongbi in taking Henan, he captured Zhengzhou and seized its defender Liu Zheng, defeated Meng Bangjie at Dengfeng, and was made defensive commissioner of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zongbi in the reconquest of Henan, he took Zhengzhou and captured its defender Liu Zheng, defeated Meng Bangjie at Dengfeng, and was appointed defensive commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 討平太行車轅嶺賊。

translations.literal: He subjugated bandits at Chexuan Ridge in the Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the bandits at Chexuan Ridge in the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 從征江南，渡淮，破孫暉兵萬餘人，下安豐、霍丘。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Jiangnan, crossing the Huai, he routed Sun Hui's force of more than ten thousand and took Anfeng and Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the south he crossed the Huai, routed Sun Hui's force of more than ten thousand, and took Anfeng and Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 及攻濠州，以彥舟為先鋒，順流薄城，擒其水軍統制邵青，遂克濠州。

translations.literal: When attacking Haozhou, Yanzhou was vanguard; going downstream he pressed the city, captured the naval commander Shao Qing, and took Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Haozhou was attacked, Yanzhou served as vanguard; sailing downstream he pressed the city, captured the naval commander Shao Qing, and took Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，累官工、兵部尚書，河南尹，封廣平郡王。

translations.literal: On return from campaign he rose to Minister of Works and of War, Henan Intendant, and was enfeoffed Duke of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he rose to minister of works and of war, intendant of Henan, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 正隆例降金紫光祿大夫，改西京留守。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Golden Violet and made Western Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was demoted to grand mentor of the golden violet and made garrison commander of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 彥舟荒於色，有禽獸行。

translations.literal: Yanzhou was dissolute in lust and had bestial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was dissolute in lust and behaved like a beast.

sentences.zh: 妾生女姿麗，彥舟苦虐其母，使自陳非己女，遂納為妾。

translations.literal: His concubine bore a daughter of striking beauty; Yanzhou cruelly abused the mother until she declared the child was not his, and he then took the girl as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine bore a daughter of striking beauty; Yanzhou cruelly abused the mother until she declared the child was not his, whereupon he took the girl as his own concubine.

sentences.zh: 其官屬負官錢，私其妻與折券。

translations.literal: When a subordinate owed official money, Yanzhou privately took his wife in exchange for canceling the debt.
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate owed official money, Yanzhou took the man's wife in private settlement of the debt.

sentences.zh: 惟破濠州時，諸軍凡系獲皆殺之，彥舟號令毋輒殺，免者數千人，人頗以此稱之。

translations.literal: Only when Haozhou was taken did he order that captives not be killed at will—several thousand were spared, and people praised him somewhat for this.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Haozhou fell did he order that captives not be killed at will—several thousand were spared, and people gave him some credit for this.

sentences.zh: 然自幼至老常在行伍，習兵事，知利鈍。

translations.literal: Yet from youth to old age he was always in the ranks, versed in military affairs and knowing when to press and when to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from youth to old age he lived in the ranks, versed in military affairs and knowing when to press and when to hold back.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲以為征南將佐，正隆五年，除南京留守。

translations.literal: Hailing wanted to use him as a southern campaign assistant; in the fifth year of Zhenglong he was made Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hailing intended to use him as an assistant in the southern campaign; in the fifth year of Zhenglong he was made garrison commander of the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 彥舟有疾，朝臣有傳彥舟死者，而彥舟尚無恙，海陵盡杖妄傳彥舟死者，以激勵之。

translations.literal: Yanzhou was ill; courtiers spread word that Yanzhou had died, though he was still alive—Hailing had everyone who falsely reported Yanzhou's death beaten with rods to spur him on.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou fell ill; courtiers spread rumors that he had died, though he was still alive—Hailing had everyone who falsely reported Yanzhou's death beaten with rods to spur him on.

sentences.zh: 無何竟死於汴，年五十五。

translations.literal: Before long he did die at Bian, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he did die at Bian, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 遺表言「伐宋當先取淮南」雲。

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated that "in attacking Song one should first take Huainan."
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he wrote that "in attacking the Song one must first take Huainan."

sentences.zh: 徐文，字彥武，萊州掖縣人，徙膠水。

translations.literal: Xu Wen, courtesy name Yanwu, was from Ye County in Laizhou, later moved to Jiaoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen, whose courtesy name was Yanwu, was from Ye County in Laizhou and later moved to Jiaoshui.

sentences.zh: 少時販鹽為業，往來瀕海數州，剛勇尚氣，儕輩皆憚之。

translations.literal: In youth he traded in salt for a living, traveling among several coastal prefectures; bold and valuing honor, his peers all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he traded in salt along several coastal prefectures; bold and quick to take offense, his peers all feared him.

sentences.zh: 宋季盜起，募戰士，為密州板橋左十將。

translations.literal: When bandits rose at the end of Song, he enlisted as a warrior and was made Left Ten General of the Board Bridge in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose at the end of the Song, he enlisted as a warrior and was made left ten-general of the Board Bridge in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 勇力過人，揮巨刀重五十斤，所向無前，人呼為「徐大刀」。

translations.literal: His courage exceeded others'; wielding a huge blade weighing fifty jin, he met no one who could stand before him, and men called him "Xu the Big Blade."
translations.idiomatic: His strength surpassed others'; wielding a great blade weighing fifty jin, he swept all before him, and men called him "Xu the Big Blade."

sentences.zh: 後隸王龍圖麾下，與夏人戰，生擒一將，補進武校尉。

translations.literal: Later he served under Wang the Academician; fighting the Xia he captured an enemy general alive and was made supplemental military cadet.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served under Academician Wang; fighting the Western Xia he captured an enemy general alive and was made supplemental military cadet.

sentences.zh: 東還，破群賊楊進等，轉承信郎。

translations.literal: Returning east, he broke the bandit Yang Jin and others and was transferred to Gentleman for Fidelity in Faith.
translations.idiomatic: Returning east, he defeated the bandits Yang Jin and others and was promoted to gentleman for fidelity in faith.

sentences.zh: 宋康王渡江，召文為樞密院準備將，擒苗傅及韓世績，以功遷淮東、浙西、沿海水軍都統制。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang of Song crossed the Yangzi, Wen was summoned as reserve general of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he captured Miao Fu and Han Shiji and, for merit, was promoted to metropolitan commander of the Huaidong, Zhexi, and coastal naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang of Song crossed the Yangzi, Wen was summoned as reserve general of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He captured Miao Fu and Han Shiji and, for his merit, was promoted to metropolitan commander of the Huaidong, Zhexi, and coastal naval forces.

sentences.zh: 諸將忌其材勇。

translations.literal: The generals envied his talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals envied his talent and courage.

sentences.zh: 是時，李成、孔彥舟皆歸齊，宋人亦疑文有北歸志，大將閻皋與文有隙，因而譖之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Cheng and Kong Yanzhou had both gone over to Qi; the Song also suspected Wen of intending to return north. The great general Yan Gao had a grudge against Wen and slandered him on that account.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Cheng and Kong Yanzhou had both defected to Qi, and the Song also suspected Wen of intending to return north. The great general Yan Gao bore a grudge against Wen and slandered him.

sentences.zh: 宋使統制硃師敏來襲文，文乃率戰艦數十艘泛海歸於齊。

translations.literal: The Song sent the commander Zhu Shimin to attack Wen; Wen then led several dozen warships across the sea and returned to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sent Commander Zhu Shimin to attack Wen, whereupon Wen led several dozen warships across the sea and defected to Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊以文為海、密二州滄海都招捉使兼水軍統制，遷海道副都統兼海道總管，賜金帶。

translations.literal: Qi made Wen coastal pacification commissioner for Hai and Mi prefectures with concurrent command of the navy, promoted him to deputy metropolitan commander and metropolitan overseer of the sea route, and bestowed a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Qi appointed Wen coastal pacification commissioner for Hai and Mi prefectures with concurrent command of the navy, promoted him to deputy metropolitan commander and metropolitan overseer of the sea route, and bestowed a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 文以策幹劉豫，欲自海道襲臨安，豫不能用。

translations.literal: Wen presented a plan to Liu Yu, wishing to strike Lin'an by sea, but Yu would not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Wen presented Liu Yu with a plan to strike Lin'an by sea, but Yu would not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，元帥府承制以文為南京步軍都虞候，權馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished, the marshal's headquarters provisionally made Wen chief adjutant of the Southern Capital infantry and acting metropolitan commander of horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished, the marshal's headquarters provisionally appointed Wen chief adjutant of the Southern Capital infantry and acting metropolitan commander of horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，破太行賊梁小哥，以本職兼水軍統制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan he defeated the Taihang bandit Liang Xiaoge and, in his existing post, was given concurrent command of the navy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 1 he defeated the Taihang bandit Liang Xiaoge and was given concurrent command of the navy in addition to his existing post.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以河南與宋，除文山東路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the court gave Henan to the Song, Wen was made military controller of Shandong East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ceded Henan to the Song, Wen was appointed military controller of Shandong East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複取河南，文破宋將李寶于濮陽、孟邦傑于登封。

translations.literal: When Zongbi retook Henan, Wen defeated the Song generals Li Bao at Puyang and Meng Bangjie at Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi retook Henan, Wen defeated the Song generals Li Bao at Puyang and Meng Bangjie at Dengfeng.

sentences.zh: 宋蔣知軍據河陽，文遲明至其城下，使別將攻城東北，自將精銳潛師襲南門。

translations.literal: The Song commander Jiang Zhi held Heyang; Wen arrived at the city at dawn, had another officer attack the northeast, and himself led picked troops in a secret assault on the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander Jiang Zhi held Heyang. Wen arrived at the city at dawn, had another officer attack the northeast, and himself led picked troops in a secret assault on the south gate.

sentences.zh: 城中悉眾救東北，文乃自南門斬關入城。

translations.literal: The city sent all its forces to rescue the northeast; Wen then broke through the south gate and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The city sent all its forces to rescue the northeast, whereupon Wen broke through the south gate and entered.

sentences.zh: 宋軍潰去，追擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Song army fled in rout; he pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army fled in rout, and he pursued and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 破郭清、郭遠於汝州。

translations.literal: He defeated Guo Qing and Guo Yuan at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Guo Qing and Guo Yuan at Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭州叛，複取之，擊走宋將戚方。

translations.literal: When Zhengzhou rebelled, he retook it and drove off the Song general Qi Fang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengzhou rebelled, he retook it and drove off the Song general Qi Fang.

sentences.zh: 河南既平，宗弼勞賞將士，賞文銀幣鞍馬。

translations.literal: When Henan was pacified, Zongbi rewarded the officers and soldiers and gave Wen silver, coins, and a saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: After Henan was pacified, Zongbi rewarded the troops and gave Wen silver, coins, and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 充行軍萬戶，從宗弼取廬、濠等州，超換武義將軍。

translations.literal: He served as campaign ten-thousand-household commander, followed Zongbi in taking Lu, Hao, and other prefectures, and was specially promoted to General of Martial Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as campaign ten-thousand-household commander, followed Zongbi in taking Lu, Hao, and other prefectures, and was specially promoted to general of martial righteousness.

sentences.zh: 知濟州，在職七年，移知泰安軍。

translations.literal: He governed Jizhou for seven years and was then transferred to govern Tai'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Jizhou for seven years and was then transferred to govern Tai'an Army.

sentences.zh: 海陵即位，錄舊功，累遷中都兵馬都指揮使，賜金帶，改浚州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Hailing took the throne, he recorded past merit; Wen was repeatedly promoted to metropolitan commander of the Central Capital military forces, bestowed a gold belt, and made defender of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing took the throne, he recorded Wen's past merit. Wen was repeatedly promoted to metropolitan commander of the Central Capital forces, bestowed a gold belt, and made defender of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，海陵謀伐宋，改行都水監，監造戰船於通州。

translations.literal: Before long, as Hailing planned war against Song, Wen was made acting director of waterways and supervised construction of warships at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as Hailing planned war against the Song, Wen was made acting director of waterways and supervised construction of warships at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 東海縣人徐元、張旺作亂，縣人房真等三人走海州，及走總管府，上變。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan and Zhang Wang of Donghai County rebelled; three men of the county, Fang Zhen and others, fled to Haizhou and then to the circuit headquarters to report the uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan and Zhang Wang of Donghai County rebelled; three local men, Fang Zhen and others, fled first to Haizhou and then to the circuit headquarters to report the uprising.

sentences.zh: 州、府皆遣使效隨真等詣東海觀賊形勢，皆為賊所害。

translations.literal: The prefecture and circuit both sent envoys following Zhen and others to Donghai to observe the rebels' situation, and all were killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and circuit both sent envoys to follow Fang Zhen and the others to Donghai to scout the rebels, and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 州、府合兵攻之，累月不下。

translations.literal: The prefecture and circuit united troops to attack but could not take them for months.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and circuit combined forces to attack them but could not take them for months.

sentences.zh: 海陵且欲伐宋，惡聞其事，詔文與步軍指揮使張弘信、同知大興尹李惟忠、宿直將軍蕭阿窊率舟師九百浮海討之，謂文等曰：「朕意不在一邑，將以試舟師耳。」

translations.literal: Hailing, who was about to attack Song and hated hearing of such disturbances, ordered Wen with Infantry Commander Zhang Hongxin, Vice Intendant of Daxing Li Weizhong, and Imperial Bodyguard Xiao A'wo to lead nine hundred warships by sea to suppress them, saying to Wen and the others: "My mind is not on one town—I mean to test the navy."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing, who was preparing to attack the Song and hated such disturbances, ordered Wen, infantry commander Zhang Hongxin, vice intendant of Daxing Li Weizhong, and imperial bodyguard Xiao A'wo to lead nine hundred warships by sea against them, telling Wen and the others, "My concern is not with one county—I mean to test the navy."

sentences.zh: 文等至東海，與賊戰，敗之，斬首五千餘級，獲徐元、張旺，餘眾請降。

translations.literal: Wen and the others reached Donghai, fought the rebels, defeated them, beheaded more than five thousand, captured Xu Yuan and Zhang Wang, and the rest surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and his party reached Donghai, fought the rebels, defeated them, beheaded more than five thousand, captured Xu Yuan and Zhang Wang, and the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是役也，張弘信行至萊州，稱疾留止，日與妓樂飲酒。

translations.literal: In this campaign Zhang Hongxin reached Laizhou, claimed illness, stayed behind, and daily drank with singers and musicians.
translations.idiomatic: During this campaign Zhang Hongxin reached Laizhou, claimed illness, and stayed behind, spending his days drinking with singers and musicians.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞之，師還，杖弘信二百。

translations.literal: When Hailing heard this, on the army's return he had Hongxin beaten two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing heard of this, on the army's return he had Hongxin beaten two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 文遷定海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Wen was transferred to military governor of the Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was promoted to military governor of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 房真三人官賞有差。

translations.literal: The three men Fang Zhen and others received differentiated offices and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhen and the other two received offices and rewards according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 死賊者皆贈官三級，以銀百兩、絹百匹賜其家。

translations.literal: Those who died fighting the rebels were all posthumously given three ranks of office, and their families were granted one hundred taels of silver and one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died fighting the rebels were all posthumously promoted three ranks, and their families were granted one hundred taels of silver and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，詣闕自陳年老目昏，懇求致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, he came to court in person, stating that he was old and his eyes dim, and earnestly requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he came to court in person, saying that he was old and his eyesight failing, and earnestly requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 以覃恩遷龍虎衛上將軍，卒于家。

translations.literal: By grace amnesty he was promoted to chief general of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: By an amnesty grant he was promoted to chief general of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and died at home.

sentences.zh: 施宜生，字明望，邵武人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yisheng, courtesy name Mingwang, was a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yisheng, whose courtesy name was Mingwang, came from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 博聞強記，未冠，由鄉貢入太學。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with a powerful memory, before coming of age he entered the Imperial Academy through the provincial tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned with a powerful memory, he entered the Imperial Academy through the provincial tribute before coming of age.

sentences.zh: 宋政和四年，擢上舍第，試學官，授潁州教授。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe of Song he ranked first among upper dormitory students, passed the academician examination, and was appointed professor at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Song Zhenghe he ranked first among upper dormitory students, passed the academician examination, and was appointed professor at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及王師入汴，宜生走江南。

translations.literal: When the royal army entered Bian, Yisheng fled to the south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army entered Bian, Yisheng fled to the south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 複以罪北走齊，上書陳取宋之策，齊以為大總管府議事官。

translations.literal: Later, fleeing north to Qi because of a crime, he submitted a memorial setting forth a plan to take Song; Qi made him deliberation officer of the grand marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fleeing north to Qi because of a crime, he submitted a memorial setting forth a plan to conquer the Song. Qi made him deliberation officer of the grand marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 失意于劉麟，左遷彰信軍節度判官。

translations.literal: Falling out with Liu Lin, he was demoted to military adjutant of the Zhangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: After falling out with Liu Lin, he was demoted to military adjutant of the Zhangxin Army.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，擢為太常博士，遷殿中侍御史，轉尚書吏部員外郎，為本部郎中。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished, he was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, transferred to palace censor, then made vice director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Department of State Affairs and director of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished, he was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, transferred to palace censor, then made vice director and bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮部，出為隰州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and sent out as prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and sent out as prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，用參知政事張浩薦宜生可備顧問，海陵召為翰林直學士，撰《太師梁王宗弼墓銘》，進官兩階。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, on the recommendation of Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Hao that Yisheng could serve as adviser, Hailing summoned him as direct academician of the Hanlin Academy; he composed the "Tomb Inscription for Grand Preceptor Prince of Liang Zongbi" and was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2, on Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Hao's recommendation that Yisheng could serve as adviser, Hailing summoned him as direct academician of the Hanlin Academy. He composed the Tomb Inscription for Grand Preceptor Prince of Liang Zongbi and was advanced two ranks.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年，出知深州，召為尚書禮部侍郎，遷翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong he was sent out to govern Shenzhou, then summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Rites of the Department of State Affairs and promoted to academician lecturer of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 1 he was sent out to govern Shenzhou, then summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Rites and promoted to academician lecturer of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，為宋國正旦使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, winter, he was New Year's envoy to the Song state.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he served as New Year's envoy to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 宜生自以得罪北走，恥見宋人，力辭，不許。

translations.literal: Yisheng, considering that he had offended and fled north, was ashamed to see Song people; he tried hard to decline but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yisheng, believing he had offended and fled north, was ashamed to face the Song; he pleaded hard to be excused but was refused.

sentences.zh: 宋命張燾館之都亭，因間以首丘風之。

translations.literal: Song appointed Zhang Tao to lodge him at Duting and in private hinted to him with the "fox's mound" sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: The Song appointed Zhang Tao to receive him at Duting and, in private, hinted that he should long for his homeland.

sentences.zh: 宜生顧其介不在旁，為廋語曰：「今日北風甚勁。」

translations.literal: Yisheng, seeing his attendant was not at his side, spoke in veiled language: "Today the north wind is very strong."
translations.idiomatic: Noticing his attendant was absent, Yisheng spoke in a double meaning: "Today the north wind blows very hard."

sentences.zh: 又取幾間筆扣之曰：「筆來，筆來。」

translations.literal: He also took a brush from the table and tapped it, saying: "The brush comes, the brush comes."
translations.idiomatic: He then took a brush from the table and tapped it, saying, "The enemy comes, the enemy comes."

sentences.zh: 於是宋始警。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song first grew alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the Song grow alarmed.

sentences.zh: 其副使耶律辟離剌使還以聞，坐是烹死。

translations.literal: His vice-envoy Yelü Bilichi reported on his return; for this [Yisheng] was boiled to death.
translations.idiomatic: His vice-envoy Yelü Bilichi reported what had happened on his return, and for this Yisheng was executed by boiling.

sentences.zh: 初，宜生困於場屋，遇僧善風鑒，謂之曰：「子面有權骨，可公可卿。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yisheng was frustrated in the examination halls, he met a monk skilled in physiognomy who said to him: "Your face has the bone of authority—you may reach duke or minister.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yisheng was struggling in the civil examinations, he met a monk skilled in reading faces who told him, "Your face bears the bone of authority—you may rise to duke or minister.

sentences.zh: 而視子身之毛，皆逆上，且覆腕，必有以合乎此而後可貴也。」

translations.literal: Yet seeing the hair on your body all grows upward, and your wrists turn back, there must be something matching this before you can become noble."
translations.idiomatic: But the hair on your body grows against the grain, and your wrists turn back—you must find something that fits this pattern before you can rise to greatness."

sentences.zh: 宜生聞其言，大喜，竟從范汝為於建、劍。

translations.literal: Hearing these words, Yisheng was greatly pleased and in the end followed Fan Ruwei in Jian and Jian circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yisheng was delighted and eventually followed Fan Ruwei in the Jian and Jian circuits.

sentences.zh: 已而汝為敗，變服為傭泰之吳翁家三年。

translations.literal: Before long Ruwei was defeated; Yisheng changed clothes and worked as a hired hand in Old Wu's household in Tai for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruwei was defeated, Yisheng disguised himself and worked as a hired laborer in Old Wu's household in Tai for three years.

sentences.zh: 翁異之，一日屏人詰其姓名，宜生曰：「我服傭事惟謹，主人乃亦置疑邪？」

translations.literal: The old man found him strange; one day he dismissed others and pressed him for his name. Yisheng said: "In my hired service I am only diligent—does my master also harbor doubts?"
translations.idiomatic: The old man found him odd; one day he sent everyone away and pressed him for his real name. Yisheng said, "I have served you diligently as a hired man—does my master doubt me too?"

sentences.zh: 翁固詰之，則請其故。

translations.literal: The old man pressed him further, so [Yisheng] asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When the old man pressed him further, Yisheng asked why.

sentences.zh: 翁曰：「日者燕客，執事咸餕，而汝獨孫諸儕，且撤器有歎聲，是以識汝非真傭也。」

translations.literal: The old man said: "The other day when entertaining guests, the attendants all served quickly, but you alone were slower than your peers, and when clearing the vessels you sighed—thus I knew you were not a true hired hand."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "When you entertained guests the other day, the other servants all hurried, but you alone lagged behind, and when you cleared the dishes you sighed—that is how I knew you were no real laborer."

sentences.zh: 宜生遂告之故。

translations.literal: Yisheng then told him the whole story.
translations.idiomatic: Yisheng then told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 翁贐之金，夜濟淮以歸。

translations.literal: The old man gave him gold as a parting gift, and by night he crossed the Huai to return.
translations.idiomatic: The old man gave him gold for the journey, and he crossed the Huai by night to return home.

sentences.zh: 試《一日獲熊三十六賦》擢第一，其後竟如僧言。

translations.literal: In the examination on "Thirty-Six Bears Taken in One Day" he was ranked first; afterward things turned out just as the monk had said.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the examination with his essay "Thirty-Six Bears Taken in One Day," and afterward everything happened just as the monk had predicted.

sentences.zh: 張中孚

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfu

sentences.zh: 張中孚，字信甫，其先自安定徙居張義堡。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfu, courtesy name Xinfu—his ancestors had moved from Anding to settle at Zhangyi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfu, whose courtesy name was Xinfu, came from a family that had moved from Anding to Zhangyi Fort.

sentences.zh: 父達，仕宋至太師，封慶國公。

translations.literal: His father Da served the Song to Grand Preceptor and was enfeoffed Duke of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da had served the Song as grand preceptor and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qing.

sentences.zh: 中孚以父任補承節郎。

translations.literal: Zhongfu entered office through his father's privilege as Gentleman for Upholding Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu entered office through his father's privilege as gentleman for upholding integrity.

sentences.zh: 宗翰圍太原，其父戰歿，中孚泣涕請跡父屍，乃獨率部曲十余人入大軍中，竟得其屍以還。

translations.literal: When Zonghan besieged Taiyuan, his father died in battle; Zhongfu wept and begged to trace his father's corpse, then alone led more than ten men of his command into the great army's camp and at last recovered the body and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan besieged Taiyuan, his father was killed in battle. Zhongfu wept and begged permission to recover the body, then led a dozen of his men alone into the Jin camp and brought his father's corpse back.

sentences.zh: 累官知鎮戎軍兼安撫使，屢從吳玠、張浚以兵拒大軍。

translations.literal: He rose to administrative chief of Zhenrong Army and concurrent pacification commissioner, repeatedly following Wu Jie and Zhang Jun with troops to resist the great army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to command Zhenrong Army and serve as pacification commissioner, repeatedly joining Wu Jie and Zhang Jun in resisting the Jin armies.

sentences.zh: 浚走巴蜀，中孚權帥事。

translations.literal: When Jun fled to Ba-Shu, Zhongfu acted as commander in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun fled to Ba-Shu, Zhongfu took command in his place.

sentences.zh: 天會八年，睿宗以左副元帥次涇州，中孚率其將吏來降，睿宗以為鎮洮軍節度使知渭州，兼涇原路經略安撫使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianhui, Prince Ruizong as left deputy marshal was stationed at Jingzhou; Zhongfu led his officers and clerks to surrender, and Ruizong made him military governor of the Zhentao Army with charge of Weizhou and concurrent Jingyuan circuit commissioner and pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianhui, Prince Ruizong was stationed at Jingzhou as left deputy marshal; Zhongfu led his officers to surrender, and Ruizong appointed him military governor of the Zhentao Army with charge of Weizhou and concurrent Jingyuan circuit commissioner and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，以什一法括民田，籍丁壯為鄉軍。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, it used the tithe law to register civilian fields and enrolled able-bodied men as local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was established, it used the tithe law to seize civilian land and enrolled able-bodied men as local militia.

sentences.zh: 中孚以為涇原地瘠無良田，且保甲之法行之已習，今遽紛更，人必逃徙，只見其害，未見其利也。

translations.literal: Zhongfu held that the Jingyuan region was barren without good fields, and that the baojia system was already practiced—if suddenly changed, people would surely flee; one would see only harm, not benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu argued that Jingyuan was barren land with no good fields, and that the baojia system was already in place—sudden changes would only drive people to flee, with harm and no benefit.

sentences.zh: 竟執不行。

translations.literal: In the end he held firm and would not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he held firm and refused to implement it.

sentences.zh: 時齊政甚急，莫敢違，人為中孚懼，而中孚不之顧。

translations.literal: At that time Qi government was very harsh and none dared disobey; people feared for Zhongfu, but he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi rule was harsh and no one dared disobey; people feared for Zhongfu, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 未幾齊國廢，一路獨免掊克之患。

translations.literal: Before long the Qi state was abolished; his circuit alone was spared the scourge of exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qi was abolished, and his circuit alone was spared the scourge of exactions.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，為陝西諸路節制使知京兆府，朝廷賜地江南，中孚遂入宋。

translations.literal: Early in Tianjuan he was circuit commissioner of Shaanxi circuits with charge of Jingzhao Prefecture; the court granted him lands south of the Yangzi, and Zhongfu then entered Song service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjuan he was circuit commissioner of Shaanxi with charge of Jingzhao Prefecture. The court granted him lands south of the Yangzi, and Zhongfu then entered Song service.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再定河南、陝西，移文宋人，使歸中孚。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again secured Henan and Shaanxi, he sent a dispatch to the Song demanding Zhongfu's return.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi again secured Henan and Shaanxi, he sent a dispatch to the Song demanding Zhongfu's return.

sentences.zh: 至汴，就除行台兵部尚書，遷除參知行台尚書省事。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Bian, he was appointed on the spot Minister of War of the Mobile Secretariat and then promoted to vice director of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Bian, he was appointed on the spot minister of war of the mobile secretariat and then promoted to vice director of the mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，遷尚書左丞，封南陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 he was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年，以疾告老，乃為濟南尹，加開府儀同三司，封宿王。

translations.literal: In the third year, citing illness he requested retirement; he was then made intendant of Jinan, granted the ceremonial regalia of the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed as Prince of Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he cited illness and requested retirement. He was then made intendant of Jinan, granted ceremonial regalia equal to the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed as Prince of Su.

sentences.zh: 移南京留守，又進封崇王。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison commander of the Southern Capital and was further enfeoffed as Prince of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison commander of the southern capital and was further enfeoffed as Prince of Chong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十九，加贈鄧王。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously advanced to Prince of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously advanced to Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 中孚天性孝友剛毅，與弟中彥居，未嘗有間言。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was by nature filial, friendly, and firm; living with his younger brother Zhongyan, they never had a harsh word between them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu was by nature filial, affectionate, and resolute; he lived with his younger brother Zhongyan and they never quarreled.

sentences.zh: 喜讀書，頗能書翰。

translations.literal: He loved reading and was quite skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading and was accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 其禦士卒嚴而有恩，西人尤畏愛之。

translations.literal: In commanding troops he was strict yet gracious; the westerners especially feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded his troops with strictness and kindness, and the people of the west especially revered and loved him.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，老稚扶柩流涕蓋數萬人，至為罷市，其得西人之望如此。

translations.literal: On the day of his burial, old and young supporting the bier wept—perhaps tens of thousands—and markets closed for it; such was the regard he won among westerners.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his burial, tens of thousands of old and young followed the coffin weeping, and markets closed in mourning—such was the esteem he won in the west.

sentences.zh: 正隆例封崇進、原國公。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was enfeoffed Duke of Chongjin and Duke of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chongjin and Duke of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 張中彥

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongyan

sentences.zh: 張中彥，字才甫，中孚弟。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongyan, courtesy name Caifu, was Zhongfu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongyan, whose courtesy name was Caifu, was Zhongfu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少以父任仕宋，為涇原副將，知德順軍事。

translations.literal: In youth through his father's privilege he served the Song as deputy general of Jingyuan and administrative chief of Deshun military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he entered Song service through his father's privilege as deputy general of Jingyuan and administrator of Deshun.

sentences.zh: 睿宗經略陝西，中彥降，除招撫使。

translations.literal: When Prince Ruizong administered Shaanxi, Zhongyan surrendered and was made pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ruizong administered Shaanxi, Zhongyan surrendered and was made pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從下熙、河、階、成州，授彰武軍承宣使，為本路兵馬鈐轄，遷都總管。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Xi, He, Jie, and Cheng prefectures, he was given honorary commissioner of the Zhangwu Army, made military controller of the circuit, and promoted to metropolitan commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the conquest of Xi, He, Jie, and Cheng prefectures, was made honorary commissioner of the Zhangwu Army and military controller of the circuit, and was promoted to metropolitan commander.

sentences.zh: 宋將關師古圍鞏州，與秦鳳李彥琦會兵攻之。

translations.literal: The Song general Guan Shigu besieged Gongzhou; [Zhongyan] joined Li Yanqi of Qin-Feng to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Guan Shigu besieged Gongzhou, Zhongyan joined Li Yanqi of Qin-Feng to attack him.

sentences.zh: 王師下饒風關，得金、洋諸州，以中彥領興元尹，撫輯新附。

translations.literal: The royal army descended on Raofeng Pass and took Jin, Yang, and other prefectures; Zhongyan was made intendant of Xingyuan to pacify the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army took Raofeng Pass and captured Jin, Yang, and other prefectures; Zhongyan was made intendant of Xingyuan to pacify the newly submitted territories.

sentences.zh: 師還，代彥琦為秦鳳經略使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he replaced Yanqi as Qin-Feng commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he replaced Yanqi as commissioner of Qin-Feng.

sentences.zh: 秦州當要衝而城不可守，中彥徙治北山，因險為壘，今秦州是也。

translations.literal: Qinzhou stood at a strategic pass but its city could not be held; Zhongyan moved the seat to North Mountain and built fortifications on the terrain—this is present-day Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou lay on a vital route but its city could not be defended; Zhongyan moved the seat to North Mountain and built fortifications on the terrain—the Qinzhou of today.

sentences.zh: 築臘家諸城，以扼蜀道。

translations.literal: He built the Lajia fortresses and others to choke the road to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Lajia fortresses and others to block the road into Shu.

sentences.zh: 帥秦凡十年，改涇原路經略使知平涼府。

translations.literal: He commanded Qin for ten years in all, then was changed to Jingyuan circuit commissioner with charge of Pingliang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Qin for ten years, then was made Jingyuan circuit commissioner with charge of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以河南、陝西賜宋，中孚以官守隨例當留關中。

translations.literal: The court ceded Henan and Shaanxi to Song; Zhongfu, by precedent as an officeholder, ought to have remained in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ceded Henan and Shaanxi to the Song, Zhongfu, as an officeholder, should by precedent have remained in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 熙河經略使慕洧謀入夏，將窺關、陝，中彥與環慶趙彬會兩路兵討之，洧敗入于夏。

translations.literal: The Xi-He commissioner Mu Wei plotted to enter Xia and was about to spy on Guan and Shaan; Zhongyan and Zhao Bin of Huanqing united troops of both circuits to attack him; Wei was defeated and fled into Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi-He commissioner Mu Wei plotted to defect to Western Xia and probe Guanzhong and Shaanxi; Zhongyan and Zhao Bin of Huanqing combined forces from both circuits to attack him; Wei was defeated and fled into Xia.

sentences.zh: 中彥與兄中孚俱至臨安，被留，以為龍神衛四廂都指揮使，清遠軍承宣使，提舉佑神觀，靖海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zhongyan and his elder brother Zhongfu both reached Lin'an and were detained, made commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, honorary commissioner of the Qingyuan Army, custodian of the Yougod Abbey, and military governor of the Jinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan and his elder brother Zhongfu both went to Lin'an and were detained, appointed commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, honorary commissioner of the Qingyuan Army, custodian of the Yougod Abbey, and military governor of the Jinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，恢復河南，詔征中彥兄弟北歸，為靜難軍節度使，曆彰化軍、鳳翔尹，改尹慶陽，兼慶原路兵馬都總管、甯州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong, when Henan was recovered, an edict summoned the Zhongyan brothers north; he was made military governor of the Jingnan Army, served as military governor of Zhanghua and intendant of Fengxiang, then intendant of Qingyang with concurrent metropolitan commander of Qingyuan circuit military forces and prefect of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangtong, when Henan was recovered, an edict summoned the brothers north; Zhongyan was made military governor of the Jingnan Army, then served as military governor of Zhanghua and intendant of Fengxiang, then intendant of Qingyang with concurrent metropolitan commander of Qingyuan forces and prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗室宗淵毆死僚佐梁鬱。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Zongyuan beat his subordinate Liang Yu to death.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Zongyuan beat his subordinate Liang Yu to death.

sentences.zh: 鬱遠人，家貧無能赴告者。

translations.literal: Yu was from afar; his family was poor and had no means to lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was an outsider from afar; his family was too poor to bring a complaint.

sentences.zh: 中彥力為正其罪，竟置於法。

translations.literal: Zhongyan strove to establish the crime and in the end had [Zongyuan] punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan pressed the case until Zongyuan was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 改彰德軍節度使，均賦調法，奸豪無所蔽匿，人服其明。

translations.literal: He was changed to military governor of the Zhangde Army, equalized tax and levy methods, and the powerful had nowhere to hide—people admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of the Zhangde Army, equalized taxes and levies, and left the powerful nowhere to hide—people admired his fairness.

sentences.zh: 正隆營汴京新宮，中彥采運關中材木。

translations.literal: During Zhenglong, when the new palace at Bianjing was built, Zhongyan gathered and transported timber from Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenglong, when the new palace at Bianjing was built, Zhongyan gathered and transported timber from Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 青峰山巨木最多，而高深阻絕，唐、宋以來不能致。

translations.literal: Qingfeng Mountain had the most giant trees, but it was deep, high, and cut off—since Tang and Song none had been able to bring them out.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfeng Mountain had the finest giant timber, but the terrain was steep and inaccessible—since Tang and Song no one had been able to bring it out.

sentences.zh: 中彥使構崖駕壑，起長橋十數裏，以車運木，若行平地，開六盤山水洛之路，遂通汴梁。

translations.literal: Zhongyan had cliffs bridged and ravines spanned, erecting long bridges for more than ten li; carts moved timber as if on level ground, opening the road from Liupan Mountain through Shuiluo, and thus reaching Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan bridged cliffs and spanned ravines, building bridges more than ten li long; carts moved timber as if on flat ground, opening the road from Liupan through Shuiluo to Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 明年，作河上浮梁，複領其役。

translations.literal: The next year a floating bridge was built on the river, and he again directed the labor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he directed construction of a floating bridge on the river.

sentences.zh: 舟之始制，匠者未得其法，中彥手制小舟才數寸許，不假膠漆而首尾自相鉤帶，謂之「鼓子卯」，諸匠無不駭服，其智巧如此。

translations.literal: When boats were first designed the craftsmen had not mastered the method; Zhongyan made by hand a small boat only a few inches long, without glue or lacquer yet bow and stern linked by themselves—called the "drum-child mortise"—and all craftsmen were awed; such was his ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: When the first boats were designed the craftsmen could not get the method right; Zhongyan made a model boat only a few inches long, with bow and stern locking together without glue or lacquer—the "drum-child mortise"—and every craftsman was astonished at his ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 浮梁巨艦畢功，將發旁郡民曳之就水。

translations.literal: When the floating bridge and great ships were finished, they were about to mobilize people from neighboring prefectures to drag them to the water.
translations.idiomatic: When the floating bridge and great ships were finished, they planned to mobilize labor from neighboring prefectures to drag them to the water.

sentences.zh: 中彥召役夫數十人，治地勢順下傾瀉於河，取新秫秸密佈於地，複以大木限其旁，淩晨督眾乘霜滑曳之，殊不勞力而致諸水。

translations.literal: Zhongyan summoned several dozen laborers, graded the ground to slope down toward the river, spread fresh sorghum stalks densely on the ground, and set large timbers along the sides; at dawn he directed the crowd to drag on the frost-slick surface—with little effort they brought them to the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan summoned several dozen laborers, graded a slope down to the river, spread fresh sorghum stalks on the ground, and set timbers along the sides; at dawn he had them drag the ships on the frost-slick surface into the water with little effort.

sentences.zh: 俄遷平陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 海陵將伐宋，驛召赴闕，授西蜀道行營副都統制，賜細鎧，使先取散關俟後命。

translations.literal: When Hailing was about to attack Song, he summoned him by post to court, appointed him deputy metropolitan commander of the Western Shu campaign headquarters, bestowed fine armor, and ordered him first to take Sanguan and await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was preparing to attack the Song, he summoned Zhongyan by post to court, appointed him deputy metropolitan commander of the Western Shu campaign headquarters, bestowed fine armor, and ordered him to take Sanguan first and await further orders.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，赦書至鳳翔，諸將惶惑不能決去就，中彥曉譬之，諸將感悟，受詔。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, the amnesty edict reached Fengxiang; the generals were fearful and could not decide whether to stay or go. Zhongyan explained and persuaded them, the generals were enlightened, and they accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, the amnesty edict reached Fengxiang. The generals were fearful and could not decide whether to stay or go, but Zhongyan explained the situation and persuaded them; they came to their senses and accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 上召中彥入朝，以軍付統軍合喜。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Zhongyan to court and entrusted the army to the commander He Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhongyan to court and entrusted the army to Commander He Xi.

sentences.zh: 及見，上賜以所禦通犀帶，封宗國公。

translations.literal: When he was received in audience, the emperor bestowed his own rhinoceros-horn belt and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zong.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, the emperor bestowed his own rhinoceros-horn belt and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zong.

sentences.zh: 尋為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「古者關市譏而不征，今使掌關市者征而不譏。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In antiquity passes and markets inspected but did not levy; now those in charge of passes and markets levy but do not inspect.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "In antiquity passes and markets were inspected but not taxed; now those in charge of passes and markets tax but do not inspect.

sentences.zh: 苛留行旅，至披剔囊笥甚於剽掠，有傷國體，乞禁止。」

translations.literal: They harshly detain travelers, even ransacking bags and cases worse than robbery—this harms the dignity of the state; I beg that it be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: They harshly detain travelers and ransack bags and cases worse than robbery, which harms the dignity of the state. I beg that this be forbidden."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 逾年，除南京留守。

translations.literal: After a year he was made Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made garrison commander of the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 時淮楚用兵，土民與戍兵雜居，訟牒紛紜，所司皆依違不決。

translations.literal: At that time Huai-Chu was at war; natives and garrison troops lived mixed together, lawsuits piled up, and the offices all wavered without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: At that time war raged in Huai-Chu; locals and garrison troops lived side by side, lawsuits piled up, and the offices wavered without deciding.

sentences.zh: 中彥得戍兵為盜者，悉論如法，帥府怒其專決，劾奏之，朝廷置而不問。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan found garrison soldiers who were thieves, he punished them all according to law; the marshal's headquarters was angry at his independent decisions and memorialized against him, but the court took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyan caught garrison soldiers who were thieves, he punished them all according to law; the marshal's headquarters was angry at his independent judgments and memorialized against him, but the court ignored it.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，轉真定尹兼河北西路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was transferred to intendant of Zhending with concurrent metropolitan commander of Hebei West Circuit military forces.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was transferred to intendant of Zhending with concurrent metropolitan commander of Hebei West Circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕，西歸京兆。

translations.literal: Before long he retired and returned west to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired and returned west to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明年，起為臨洮尹兼熙秦路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled as intendant of Lintao with concurrent metropolitan commander of Xi-Qin circuit military forces.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as intendant of Lintao with concurrent metropolitan commander of Xi-Qin forces.

sentences.zh: 鞏州劉海構亂，既敗，籍民之從亂者數千人，中彥惟論為首者戮之。

translations.literal: Liu Hai of Gongzhou plotted rebellion; after he was defeated, several thousand civilians who had joined the rebellion were registered—Zhongyan punished only the ringleaders with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hai of Gongzhou plotted rebellion; after his defeat, several thousand civilians who had joined were registered—Zhongyan executed only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 西羌吹折、密臧、隴逋、龐拜四族恃險不服，使侍御史沙醇之就中彥論方略，中彥曰：「此羌服叛不常，若非中彥自行，勢必不可。」

translations.literal: The four western Qiang clans Suizhe, Mizang, Longbu, and Pangbai relied on terrain and would not submit; the attendant censor Sha Chunzhi was sent to Zhongyan to discuss strategy. Zhongyan said: "These Qiang submit and rebel without constancy—unless Zhongyan goes in person, the situation surely cannot be settled."
translations.idiomatic: The four western Qiang clans Suizhe, Mizang, Longbu, and Pangbai held difficult terrain and refused submission; attendant censor Sha Chunzhi was sent to consult Zhongyan. Zhongyan said, "These Qiang submit and rebel without pattern—unless I go in person, it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 即至積石達南寺，酋長四人來，與之約降，事遂定，賞而遣之。

translations.literal: He then reached Jishi and arrived at Nan Monastery; the four chieftains came, made a pact to surrender with him, the matter was settled, and he rewarded and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jishi and reached Nan Monastery; the four chieftains came, agreed to surrender, the matter was settled, and he rewarded and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 還奏，上大悅，遣張汝玉馳驛勞之，賜以球文金帶，用郊恩加儀同三司。

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized; the emperor was greatly pleased, sent Zhang Ruyu by post horse to comfort him, granted a ball-pattern gold belt, and by suburban grace added Honorary Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported to the throne; the emperor was delighted, sent Zhang Ruyu by post horse to reward him, granted a ball-pattern gold belt, and by suburban grace promoted him to honorary three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒官，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died in office from illness at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office from illness at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 百姓哀號輟市，立像祀之。

translations.literal: The common people wailed and closed their markets; they set up images to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people wailed in grief and closed their markets; they set up images to worship him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：自古健將武夫，其不才者，遭世變遷，賣降恐後。

translations.literal: The praise says: From antiquity among stalwart generals and warriors, the untalented, when the age changed, sold surrender and feared to be last.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Throughout history, among bold generals and warriors, the untalented, when times changed, rushed to surrender and feared to be last.

sentences.zh: 此其常態，君子之所不責也，酈瓊、徐文是已。

translations.literal: This is their constant pattern—what gentlemen do not blame—and Li Qiong and Xu Wen are examples.
translations.idiomatic: That is their usual pattern, which gentlemen do not condemn—and Li Qiong and Xu Wen are cases in point.

sentences.zh: 施宜生反覆壬人，李成盜賊之靡，孔彥舟漁色親出，自絕人類，又何責也。

translations.literal: Shi Yisheng was a fickle man of craft; Li Cheng was a bandit's wastrel; Kong Yanzhou preyed on beauty and took his own kin—having cut themselves off from humanity, what further blame is there?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yisheng was a fickle schemer; Li Cheng a bandit's wastrel; Kong Yanzhou preyed on beauty and took his own kin—they had cut themselves off from humanity, and what more is there to blame?

sentences.zh: 張中孚、中彥雖有小惠足稱，然以宋大臣之子，父戰沒于金，若金若齊，義皆不共戴天之仇。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfu and Zhongyan, though they had small kindnesses worth praise, were sons of a Song great minister whose father died in battle against Jin—whether Jin or Qi, in righteousness both were enemies with whom one cannot share the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfu and Zhongyan, though they had small virtues worth noting, were sons of a Song minister whose father died fighting the Jin—whether toward Jin or Qi, by righteousness both were mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 金以地與齊則甘心臣齊，以地歸宋則忍恥臣宋，金取其地則又比肩臣金，若趨市然，唯利所在，于斯時也，豈複知所謂綱常也哉。

translations.literal: When Jin gave land to Qi they gladly served Qi; when land returned to Song they bore shame and served Song; when Jin took the land they again stood shoulder to shoulder as Jin subjects, like hurrying to market—wherever profit lay. At such a time, how could they still know what is called moral order?
translations.idiomatic: When Jin gave land to Qi they gladly served Qi; when land went back to Song they swallowed shame and served Song; when Jin took the land they served Jin again side by side, like men rushing to market—wherever profit led. In such times, how could they still know moral principle?

sentences.zh: 籲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 宇文虛中，字叔通，蜀人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xuzhong, courtesy name Shutong, was a man of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xuzhong, whose courtesy name was Shutong, was a man of Shu.
