sentences.zh: 初仕宋，累官資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: He first served the Song and rose to Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Song and rose to grand academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，宋少帝已結盟，宗望班師至孟陽，宋姚平仲乘夜來襲，明日複進兵圍汴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui the Song Lesser Emperor had already made alliance; Zongwang withdrew his army to Mengyang; the Song general Yao Pingzhong attacked by night, and the next day advanced again to besiege Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 4 the Song Lesser Emperor had already made alliance. Zongwang withdrew his army to Mengyang, where the Song general Yao Pingzhong attacked by night; the next day he advanced again to besiege Bian.

sentences.zh: 少帝使虛中詣宗望軍，告以襲兵皆將帥自為之，複請和議如初，且視康王安否。

translations.literal: The Lesser Emperor sent Xuzhong to Zongwang's army, reporting that the night attack had been the generals' own doing, again requesting peace talks as before, and also asking whether Prince Kang was safe.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Emperor sent Xuzhong to Zongwang's army, reporting that the night attack had been the generals' own doing, again requesting peace talks as before, and also asking whether Prince Kang was safe.

sentences.zh: 頃之，台諫以和議歸罪虛中，罷為青州，複下遷祠職。

translations.literal: Before long the censors blamed Xuzhong for the peace talks; he was dismissed to Qingzhou and then further demoted to a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the censors blamed Xuzhong for the peace talks. He was dismissed to Qingzhou and then further demoted to a temple post.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，貶韶州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was banished to Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 he was banished to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，康王求可為奉使者，虛中自貶中應詔，複資政殿大學士，為祈請使。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Kang sought someone who could serve as tribute envoy; Xuzhong answered the edict from exile, was restored as Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance, and made petitioning envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Prince Kang sought someone who could serve as tribute envoy. Xuzhong answered the edict from exile, was restored as grand academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance, and made petitioning envoy.

sentences.zh: 是時，興兵伐宋，已留王倫、硃弁不遣，虛中亦被留，實天會六年也。

translations.literal: At that time war against Song had been raised; Wang Lun and Zhu Bian had already been detained and not sent back, and Xuzhong was detained as well—this was in fact the sixth year of Tianhui.
translations.idiomatic: At that time war against the Song had been raised. Wang Lun and Zhu Bian had already been detained and not sent back, and Xuzhong was detained as well—in fact Tianhui 6.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方議禮制度，頗愛虛中有才藝，加以官爵，虛中即受之，與韓昉輩俱掌詞命。

translations.literal: The court was then debating ritual institutions and rather admired Xuzhong's talent and skill; offices and ranks were added, and Xuzhong accepted them at once, joining Han Fang and others in managing edicts and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then debating ritual institutions and admired Xuzhong's talent. Offices and ranks were added, and Xuzhong accepted them at once, joining Han Fang and others in managing edicts and appointments.

sentences.zh: 明年，洪皓至上京，見虛中，甚鄙之。

translations.literal: The next year Hong Hao reached Shangjing, saw Xuzhong, and despised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hong Hao reached Shangjing, saw Xuzhong, and despised him greatly.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年，熙宗即位。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui Xizong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 13 Xizong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 宗翰為太保領三省事，封晉國王，乞致仕。

translations.literal: Zonghan was Grand Guardian heading the Three Departments, enfeoffed as Prince of Jin, and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was grand guardian heading the Three Departments, enfeoffed as Prince of Jin, and requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 批答不允，其詞虛中作也。

translations.literal: The written reply refusing permission was composed by Xuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The written reply refusing permission was composed by Xuzhong.

sentences.zh: 天眷間，累官翰林學士知制誥兼太常卿，封河內郡開國公。

translations.literal: During Tianjuan he rose through posts to Hanlin academician, controller of edicts, and concurrent director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was enfeoffed as Duke of the Henan commandery state.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjuan he rose to Hanlin academician, controller of edicts, and concurrent director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was enfeoffed as duke of the Henan commandery state.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，宋人請和，其誓表曰：「自來流移在南之人，經官陳說，願自歸者，更不禁止。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong the Song sought peace; their oath memorial said: "People who have drifted south in the past, having stated their case to officials and wishing to return of their own accord, shall no longer be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 the Song sought peace. Their oath memorial said, "People who have drifted south in the past, having stated their case to officials and wishing to return of their own accord, shall no longer be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 上國之於弊邑，亦乞並用此約。」

translations.literal: As for our humble state, we also beg that the supreme state apply this same agreement."
translations.idiomatic: As for our humble state, we also beg that the supreme state apply this same agreement."

sentences.zh: 於是，詔尚書省移文宋國，理索張中孚、張中彥、鄭億年、杜充、張孝純、宇文虛中、王進家屬，發遣李正民、畢良史還宋，惟孟庾去留聽其所欲。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to send a dispatch to the Song state demanding the families of Zhang Zhongfu, Zhang Zhongyan, Zheng Yinian, Du Chong, Zhang Xiaochun, Yuwen Xuzhong, and Wang Jin, and to send Li Zhengmin and Bi Liangshi back to the Song; only Meng Yu's going or staying was left to his own wish.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to send a dispatch to the Song demanding the families of Zhang Zhongfu, Zhang Zhongyan, Zheng Yinian, Du Chong, Zhang Xiaochun, Yuwen Xuzhong, and Wang Jin, and to send Li Zhengmin and Bi Liangshi back to the Song. Only whether Meng Yu went or stayed was left to his own wish.

sentences.zh: 時虛中子師瑗仕宋，至轉運判官，攜家北來。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhong's son Shi Yuan served the Song, rising to transport vice commissioner, and brought his family north.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuzhong's son Shi Yuan served the Song, rising to transport vice commissioner, and brought his family north.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉承旨，加特進。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to drafting director and granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to drafting director and granted special advancement.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，承旨如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Rites while retaining his post as drafting director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of rites while retaining his post as drafting director.

sentences.zh: 虛中恃才輕肆，好譏訕，凡見女直人輒以礦鹵目之，貴人達官往往積不能平。

translations.literal: Xuzhong relied on talent and was lightly reckless, fond of mockery; whenever he saw Jurchen he would regard them as crude salt-works, and eminent officials often nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhong relied on his talent and was reckless and mocking; whenever he saw Jurchens he treated them with contempt, and eminent officials often nursed deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 虛中嘗撰宮殿榜署，本皆嘉美之名，惡虛中者擿其字以為謗訕朝廷，由是媒糵以成其罪矣。

translations.literal: Xuzhong once composed palace inscriptions—all originally auspicious names—but those who hated him picked out characters as slander of the court, and thus framed charges to complete his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhong once composed palace inscriptions—all originally auspicious names—but his enemies twisted the characters into slander of the court, and thus fabricated charges against him.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，唐括酬斡家奴杜天佛留告虛中謀反，詔有司鞫治無狀，乃羅織虛中家圖書為反具，虛中曰：「死自吾分。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, Tangguo Chouwo's household slave Du Tianfoliu reported that Xuzhong plotted rebellion; an edict ordered the offices to investigate and found no substance, so they fabricated Xuzhong's household books as evidence of rebellion. Xuzhong said: "Death is my portion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year, Tangguo Chouwo's slave Du Tianfoliu accused Xuzhong of plotting rebellion; the court ordered an investigation and found no case, so they fabricated evidence from Xuzhong's household books. Xuzhong said, "Death is my portion.

sentences.zh: 至於圖籍，南來士大夫家家有之，高士談圖書尤多於我家，豈亦反耶？」

translations.literal: As for books, every southern gentleman who came north has them; Gao Shitan's books are even more numerous than mine—are they rebels too?"
translations.idiomatic: As for books, every southern gentleman who came north has them; Gao Shitan's library is even larger than mine—is he a rebel too?"

sentences.zh: 有司承順風旨並殺士談，至今冤之。

translations.literal: The offices, following the prevailing intent, killed Shitan as well; to this day he is regarded as wronged.
translations.idiomatic: The offices, following the prevailing wind, killed Shitan as well—to this day he is regarded as wronged.

sentences.zh: 士談字季默，高瓊之後。

translations.literal: Shitan, courtesy name Jimo, was a descendant of Gao Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Shitan, whose courtesy name was Jimo, was a descendant of Gao Qiong.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，為忻州戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe he was revenue clerk of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe period he was revenue clerk of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 入朝，官至翰林直學士。

translations.literal: He entered court service and rose to Hanlin Academician Expectant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service and rose to Hanlin academician expectant.

sentences.zh: 虛中、士談俱有文集行於世。

translations.literal: Xuzhong and Shitan both had collected writings circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Both Xuzhong and Shitan left collected writings that circulated in their day.

sentences.zh: 王倫，字正道，故宋宰相王旦弟王勉玄孫。

translations.literal: Wang Lun, courtesy name Zhengdao, was the great-great-grandson of Wang Mian, younger brother of the former Song chancellor Wang Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun, whose courtesy name was Zhengdao, was the great-great-grandson of Wang Mian, younger brother of the former Song chancellor Wang Dan.

sentences.zh: 俠邪無賴，年四十余尚與市井惡少群游汴中。

translations.literal: Rakish and worthless, past forty he still roamed Bian with the town's rowdy youths.
translations.idiomatic: Rakish and worthless, past forty he still roamed Bian with the town's rowdy youths.

sentences.zh: 天會五年，宋人以倫為假刑部侍郎，與閣門舍人硃弁充通問使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhui, the Song made Lun acting vice minister of justice and, with Palace Gate Attendant Zhu Bian, envoys for communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianhui, the Song appointed Lun acting vice minister of justice and, with palace gate attendant Zhu Bian, envoys to open communications.

sentences.zh: 是時，方議伐宋，凡宋使者如倫及宇文虛中、魏行可、顧縱、張邵等，皆留之不遣。

translations.literal: At that time they were debating war against Song; all Song envoys such as Lun, Yu Wen Xuzhong, Wei Xingke, Gu Zong, Zhang Shao, and others were detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: At that time war against the Song was under discussion; all Song envoys such as Lun, Yuwen Xuzhong, Wei Xingke, Gu Zong, and Zhang Shao were detained and not sent back.

sentences.zh: 居數年，倫久困，乃唱為和議求歸。

translations.literal: After several years, Lun long distressed, then advocated peace talks to seek return.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in detention, Lun, long distressed, began advocating peace talks in order to return home.

sentences.zh: 元帥府使人謂之曰：「此非江南情實，特汝自為此言耳。」

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters sent someone to say to him: "This is not the true situation in Jiangnan—you are only speaking for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters sent someone to tell him, "That is not the true situation in the south—you are only speaking for yourself."

sentences.zh: 倫曰：「使事有指，不然何為來哉。

translations.literal: Lun said: "An envoy's mission has its aim—otherwise why come?
translations.idiomatic: Lun said, "An envoy's mission has its purpose—otherwise why would I have come?

sentences.zh: 惟元帥察之。」

translations.literal: Only let the marshal discern it."
translations.idiomatic: Only let the marshal judge for himself."

sentences.zh: 天會十年，劉豫連歲出師皆無功，撻懶為元帥左監軍經略南邊，密主和議，乃遣倫歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianhui, Liu Yu's campaigns year after year were all fruitless; Tadun was left supervising general of the marshal's army administering the south and secretly favored peace talks, and so sent Lun back.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianhui, Liu Yu's campaigns had failed year after year; Tadun, left supervising general on the southern front, secretly favored peace talks and sent Lun back.

sentences.zh: 先此，宋已遣使乞和，朝廷未之許也。

translations.literal: Before this, Song had already sent envoys begging peace, but the court had not granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the Song had already sent envoys begging for peace, but the court had not agreed.

sentences.zh: 倫見康王言和議事，康王大喜，遷倫官，並官其子弟。

translations.literal: Lun saw Prince Kang and spoke of peace talks; Prince Kang was greatly pleased, promoted Lun's office, and also gave offices to his sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Lun met Prince Kang and spoke of peace talks; the prince was delighted, promoted Lun, and gave offices to his sons and younger brothers as well.

sentences.zh: 宋方與齊用兵，未可和。

translations.literal: Song was just then at war with Qi—peace was not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: The Song was still at war with Qi, so peace was not yet possible.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，康王聞天水郡王已薨，以倫假直學士來請其喪，使倫請撻懶曰：「河南之地，上國既不自有，與其封劉豫，曷若歸之趙氏？」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, Prince Kang heard that the Prince of Tianshui had died and sent Lun, acting direct academician, to request the coffin; Lun was made to ask Tadun: "The lands of Henan—since the supreme state does not keep them for itself, rather than enfeoffing Liu Yu, would it not be better to return them to the house of Zhao?"
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15, Prince Kang heard that the Prince of Tianshui had died and sent Lun, acting direct academician, to request the coffin. Lun was told to ask Tadun, "The lands of Henan—since the supreme state does not keep them for itself, rather than enfeoffing Liu Yu, would it not be better to return them to the house of Zhao?"

sentences.zh: 是歲，劉豫受封已八年，不能自立其國，尚勤屯戍，朝廷厭其無能為也，乃廢劉豫。

translations.literal: That year Liu Yu had held his enfeoffment for eight years, could not establish his state on his own, and still kept garrisons busy; the court was weary of his uselessness and abolished Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Yu had held his enfeoffment for eight years but could not establish his state on his own and still kept garrisons busy. The court was weary of his uselessness and abolished him.

sentences.zh: 撻懶以左副元帥守汴京，於是倫適至。

translations.literal: Tadun was left deputy marshal guarding Bianjing, and Lun happened to arrive just then.
translations.idiomatic: Tadun was left deputy marshal guarding Bianjing, and Lun happened to arrive just then.

sentences.zh: 撻懶，太祖從父兄弟，于熙宗為祖行。

translations.literal: Tadun was a paternal cousin of Taizu and, to Xizong, stood one generation above him in seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Tadun was a paternal cousin of Taizu and, to Xizong, stood one generation above him in seniority.

sentences.zh: 太宗長子宗磐乙太師領三省事，位在宗幹上。

translations.literal: Taizong's eldest son Zongpan, as Grand Preceptor, headed the Three Departments and ranked above Zonggan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's eldest son Zongpan, as grand preceptor, headed the Three Departments and ranked above Zonggan.

sentences.zh: 宗翰薨已久，宗幹不能與宗磐獨抗。

translations.literal: Zonghan had long since died; Zonggan could not stand alone against Zongpan.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan had long since died, and Zonggan could not stand alone against Zongpan.

sentences.zh: 明年，天眷元年，撻懶與東京留守宗雋俱入朝，熙宗以宗雋為左丞相。

translations.literal: The next year, the first year of Tianjuan, Tadun and the Eastern Capital regent Zongjun both entered court; Xizong made Zongjun left chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, Tianjuan 1, Tadun and Eastern Capital regent Zongjun both entered court. Xizong made Zongjun left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 宗雋，太祖子也。

translations.literal: Zongjun was a son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjun was a son of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 撻懶、宗磐、宗雋三人皆跋扈嗜利，陰有異圖，遂合議以齊地與宋，自宗幹以下爭之不能得。

translations.literal: Tadun, Zongpan, and Zongjun were all overbearing and greedy for profit, secretly harboring other designs; they therefore agreed together to give Qi's lands to the Song, and from Zonggan downward all disputed it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Tadun, Zongpan, and Zongjun were all overbearing and greedy for profit and secretly harbored other designs. They therefore agreed to give Qi's lands to the Song, and from Zonggan downward all disputed it but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 以侍郎張通古為詔諭江南使，遣倫先歸。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhang Tonggu was made edict-announcing envoy to Jiangnan, and Lun was sent back first.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhang Tonggu was made edict-announcing envoy to Jiangnan, and Lun was sent back first.

sentences.zh: 明年，宋以倫為端明殿學士，簽書樞密院事，進金器千兩、銀器萬兩，複來請天水郡王喪柩，及請母韋氏兄弟宗族等。

translations.literal: The next year Song made Lun Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, presented one thousand taels of gold vessels and ten thousand taels of silver vessels, and again came to request the coffin of the Prince of Tianshui and to request his mother Lady Wei, brothers, clansmen, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Song appointed Lun academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, presented one thousand taels of gold vessels and ten thousand taels of silver vessels, and again came to request the coffin of the Prince of Tianshui and the return of his mother Lady Wei, his brothers, and his clansmen.

sentences.zh: 保信軍節度使藍公佐副之。

translations.literal: Lan Gongzuo, military governor of the Baoxin Army, served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Gongzuo, military governor of the Baoxin Army, served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 是歲，宗磐、宗雋、撻懶皆以謀反屬吏，熙宗誅宗磐、宗雋，以撻懶屬尊，赦其死，以為行台尚書省事左丞相，奪其兵權。

translations.literal: That year Zongpan, Zongjun, and Tadun were all implicated in rebellion by subordinates; Emperor Xizong executed Zongpan and Zongjun; because Tadun was of honored lineage he pardoned his death, made him left chancellor of the Mobile Secretariat, and stripped his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zongpan, Zongjun, and Tadun were all implicated in rebellion; Emperor Xizong executed Zongpan and Zongjun, but because Tadun was of honored lineage he spared his life, made him left chancellor of the mobile secretariat, and stripped him of military authority.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥宗弼奏曰：「撻懶、宗磐陰與宋人交通，遂以河南、陝西地與宋人。」

translations.literal: Right deputy marshal Zongbi memorialized: "Tadun and Zongpan secretly communicated with the Song and thus gave Henan and Shaanxi to the Song."
translations.idiomatic: Right deputy marshal Zongbi memorialized, "Tadun and Zongpan secretly communicated with the Song and gave Henan and Shaanxi to them."

sentences.zh: 會撻懶複謀反，捕而殺之于祁州。

translations.literal: When Tadun again plotted rebellion, he was captured and killed at Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tadun plotted rebellion again, he was captured and killed at Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 倫至上京，有司詳讀康王表文，不書年，閱進奉狀，稱禮物不言職貢，上使宰相責問倫曰：「汝但知有元帥，豈知有上國耶。」

translations.literal: Lun reached Shangjing; the offices read Prince Kang's memorial in detail—it did not record the year; examining the tribute presentation, it called them "gifts" and did not say "tribute." The emperor had the chancellor rebuke Lun: "You only know there is a marshal—do you not know there is a supreme state?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lun reached Shangjing, the offices examined Prince Kang's memorial in detail—it bore no year; the tribute presentation called them "gifts" rather than "tribute." The emperor had the chancellor rebuke Lun: "You know only the marshal—do you not know there is a supreme state?"

sentences.zh: 遂留不遣，遣其副藍公佐歸。

translations.literal: He was then detained and not sent back; his deputy Lan Gongzuo was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was detained and not sent back; only his deputy Lan Gongzuo was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，宗弼複取河南、陝西地，遂伐江南，已渡淮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Zongbi again took the lands of Henan and Shaanxi, then campaigned against Jiangnan and had already crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, Zongbi again took Henan and Shaanxi, then campaigned against Jiangnan and had already crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年，宋人請和。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangtong the Song sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 1 the Song sought peace.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，宋端明殿學士何鑄、容州觀察使曹勳進誓表。

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, the Song academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity He Zhu and military commissioner of Rongzhou Cao Xun presented the oath memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, Song academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity He Zhu and military commissioner of Rongzhou Cao Xun presented the oath memorial.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣左副點檢賽裏、山東西路都轉運使劉祹送天水郡王喪柩，及宋帝母韋氏還江南。

translations.literal: In the third month, Left Deputy Inspector Saili and metropolitan transport commissioner of Shandong East and West Circuits Liu Ni were sent to escort the coffin of the Prince of Tianshui and Lady Wei, mother of the Song emperor, back to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Left Deputy Inspector Saili and metropolitan transport commissioner of Shandong East and West Circuits Liu Ni were sent to escort the coffin of the Prince of Tianshui and Lady Wei, mother of the Song emperor, back to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 五月，李正明、畢良史南歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Li Zhengming and Bi Liangshi returned south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Li Zhengming and Bi Liangshi returned south.

sentences.zh: 七月，硃弁、張邵、洪皓南歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zhu Bian, Zhang Shao, and Hong Hao returned south.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Zhu Bian, Zhang Shao, and Hong Hao returned south.

sentences.zh: 四年，以倫為平州路轉運使，倫已受命，複辭遜，上曰：「此反復之人也。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year Lun was made transport commissioner of Pingzhou Circuit; Lun had already accepted the appointment but again declined humbly. The emperor said: "This is a fickle man."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Lun was appointed transport commissioner of Pingzhou Circuit; he had already accepted the post but declined again. The emperor said, "This is a fickle man."

sentences.zh: 遂殺之於上京，年六十一。

translations.literal: He was then killed at Shangjing, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was then executed at Shangjing, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孔子雲：「行己有恥，使于四方不辱君命，可謂士矣」。

translations.literal: The praise says: Confucius said, "In conduct one has shame; sent to the four directions one does not disgrace the ruler's charge—such a one may be called a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Confucius said, "To conduct oneself with a sense of shame, and when sent abroad not to disgrace one's ruler's commission—that is what may be called a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 宇文虛中朝至上京，夕受官爵。

translations.literal: Yu Wen Xuzhong reached Shangjing in the morning and received office and rank by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xuzhong reached Shangjing in the morning and accepted office and rank by evening.

sentences.zh: 王倫紈袴之子，市井為徒。

translations.literal: Wang Lun was a silk-trousered son who consorted with the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun was a spoiled scion who ran with the marketplace rabble.

sentences.zh: 此豈「行己有恥」之士，可以專使者耶？

translations.literal: How could such men be gentlemen who "in conduct have shame," fit to serve as sole envoys?
translations.idiomatic: How could such men be gentlemen "who conduct themselves with shame," fit to serve as sole envoys?

sentences.zh: 二子之死雖冤，其自取亦多矣。

translations.literal: Though the deaths of these two men were wrongful, they had also brought much upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Though the deaths of these two men were wrongful, they had also brought much of it upon themselves.
